title: RAID: Shadow Legends Alice Fan Art Reinterpreted Through the Detailed Synergy of Marvelous Designer and ZBrush
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/228a434ffe934adb90c9dcd52c0d9b7a02.jpg)

![f7971c632dbc401ea5f52320895e7f0a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/f7971c632dbc401ea5f52320895e7f0a17.jpg)  
Introducing 3D character artist [Dahye Han](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/V8gQ9g)'s workflow for her _RAID: Shadow Legends Alice_ fan art—rapidly capturing garment silhouettes using Marvelous Designer's intuitive simulation, then perfecting realistic textures and layered details with ZBrush and Substance Painter.

**Software used:**

  * ZBrush - Sculpting

  * 3ds Max - Modeling & Retopology & UV-Unwrapping & Ornatrix

  * Marvelous Designer - Cloth simulation

  * Substance 3D Painter - Texturing

  * Marmoset Toolbag - Baking & Lighting & Rendering

  * Photoshop - Retouching




#   
**Artist Introduction**

Hello! My name is Dahye Han.

After graduating with a degree in Industrial Design, I worked as an advertising designer before developing an interest in character modeling out of a desire to create characters I personally love. This inspired me to pursue serious study in the field, building up my skills while creating portfolios based on what I learned.

# **Project Introduction**

This project is a fan art piece of Alice from _RAID: Shadow Legends_.

I was drawn to the alluring and dark atmosphere of the original concept art. My goal was to retain the original concept and key character traits while adding realistic textures and intricate details to reinterpret her with a sense of vitality.![2b01473edd5a4d479f154d4b744cc71b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/2b01473edd5a4d479f154d4b744cc71b02.jpg)

# **Tell us how Marvelous Designer creates value in this project.**

In this project, I used Marvelous Designer during garment creation whenever it was difficult to express natural folds using ZBrush sculpting alone.

First, I established the overall silhouette and the main direction of the major folds in Marvelous Designer. Then, I refined the flow of the wrinkles and the silhouette using ZBrush's Dynamics feature and sculpting. Finally, I added textures and details appropriate for each fabric material in Substance Painter to enhance the overall level of completion.

![1d5a21175a0949969c96f4a8b7c909f9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/1d5a21175a0949969c96f4a8b7c909f905.jpg)![06c94db460d2466cbc12905b4be9286b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/06c94db460d2466cbc12905b4be9286b06.jpg)![8ae394b71b234d5684a8213d4da8867a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/8ae394b71b234d5684a8213d4da8867a07.jpg)![ce1e65d8ea114b36babb2d8edae83e0e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/ce1e65d8ea114b36babb2d8edae83e0e08.jpg)![eeef15be2b2846ce99ea9683898d72a4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/eeef15be2b2846ce99ea9683898d72a409.jpg)![1092ab717a5e4572af69992d6abab51f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/1092ab717a5e4572af69992d6abab51f10.jpg)![c564274bc60242108608514eb284f8a3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/c564274bc60242108608514eb284f8a311.jpg)![f94ff0e910d84f0487b14c494365c901](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/f94ff0e910d84f0487b14c494365c90112.jpg)

# **What is your favorite feature or tool to use in Marvelous Designer?**

My favorite feature is the simulation tool.

Compared to simulation features in other software, it has an intuitive UI, fast workflow, and allows me to inspect and adjust garment shapes and folds directly in real time. I rely on it heavily during the initial shaping phase, as it enables me to quickly establish the overall silhouette and the flow of the wrinkles.

# **The clothing layers and various trim details really stand out. Please tell us about what you focused on or your production process when working in Marvelous Designer.**

When creating the skirt in Marvelous Designer, I paid close attention to expressing the natural, flowing silhouette of the double-layered skirt and the apron.

Because the inner and outer skirts had different designs, I created a pleated skirt and a flared skirt separately in Marvelous Designer to establish a natural shape. Afterwards, I refined the overall silhouette and wrinkles in ZBrush before adding fine details.

To express the clover pattern at the bottom of the apron as a structured trim, I applied the pattern as an alpha aligned to the UV space in ZBrush, cleaned up the area using masking, and finished it by adding thickness and detail.

# ![4eb70ddfd37d46b88724950cab335af0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/4eb70ddfd37d46b88724950cab335af013.jpg)![3d16d97704c84182a03de99d231abbd1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/3d16d97704c84182a03de99d231abbd114.jpg)![71f5084b739f4201a647d17c8adb9d93](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/71f5084b739f4201a647d17c8adb9d9315.jpg)![348f85a1e2354763ad8dbd6c559acf58](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/348f85a1e2354763ad8dbd6c559acf5816.jpg)![eb007d919e0e421cab55646bf574ddf8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/d6037215d3344ab295b0a4bcd3c171e2/images/eb007d919e0e421cab55646bf574ddf801.jpg)

# **For other users considering Marvelous Designer, do you have any advice or experience to share?**

When I first started using Marvelous Designer, I wasn't familiar with how to construct and create garment patterns. However, there are many tutorial videos on the official YouTube channel explaining the workflow in detail, along with a wide variety of reference materials. Following along step by step helped me get comfortable with the software naturally and allowed me to enjoy the process of making clothing.

Now, I use it to quickly construct necessary outfit pieces and refine them while inspecting the shape in real time. Rather than trying to create a perfect pattern from the start, I think starting with simple forms and repeating simulations is the best way to master the software.
content_description: This webpage showcases 3D character artist Dahye Han’s detailed workflow and techniques using Marvelous Designer and other tools to create realistic garment simulations and textures for her _RAID: Shadow Legends Alice_ fan art.

title: Fabric as Storytelling in The Abandoned Orphanage
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/38ee6a11a70241a3b75261dc4c048c18Ana%20Vien%20-%20Square.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/b6a2933703e84f9e903c5fe04fa01b69Ana%20Vien%20-%20Square.png)![cc0d08373b9d49c7ae4df3ef432d9e94](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/cc0d08373b9d49c7ae4df3ef432d9e9404%20%281%29.png)

## _3D Environment Artist_[ _Ana Vien_](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/gRZE4K) _shares how Marvelous Designer helped bring believable fabric, aged curtains, and quiet narrative detail into her real-time scene, The Abandoned Orphanage._

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ey5BBcD1GWc

* * *

**Software Used**

  * Blender - Modeling

  * Marvelous Designer - Cloth Simulation

  * Substance Painter - Texturing

  * Unreal Engine - Lighting & Rendering




* * *

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and your current focus as a 3D Environment Artist?**

Hi everyone, my name is Ana, and I'm a 3D Environment Artist. My current focus is level art: building spaces with strong visual composition and storytelling at their core.

# **Could you introduce _The Abandoned Orphanage_ and share how the idea evolved during production?**

At first, the project consisted of a single corridor. It was created for The Rookies: Shadows challenge and featured the ghosts of children. At that stage, the scene only showed subtle signs of abandonment, the passage of time, and complete silence. However, it was still quite unpolished.

I didn't want the orphanage to feel too luxurious or overly dark. Instead, I wanted it to feel mysterious and dangerous.

I spent another month adding a children's bedroom and an assembly hall while improving the environmental storytelling.

![0069735d289b4e32baf9cd9975294ba5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/0069735d289b4e32baf9cd9975294ba501%20%281%29.png)

# **The scene includes many narrative details, from children's objects to torn fabrics and overgrown organic forms. How did you decide what to include?**

In the bedroom, I tried to show each child's personality through their belongings. Despite their differences, they all shared the same wish: to have a family. On the floor, they created something that looked like a ritual, hoping it would bring them one.

A mysterious organic growth spreads across the ceiling. It represents the grief and tragedy that had built up in the room over the years, slowly spreading throughout the orphanage.

I visually divided the assembly hall into two parts. One side of the stage represents death and decay, while the other represents life. In a way, the stage reflects life itself.

![9f96e7c169e644feaf64a31a76d18486](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/9f96e7c169e644feaf64a31a76d1848602%20%281%29.png)

This idea can be seen through the paintings, plants, animals, and music. Tchaikovsky's _The Sick Doll_ perfectly matches the mood of the scene. Many of the sheet music pages are simple piano lessons for children, showing that this room was once a place where they learned and spent time together.

I wanted the curtains to look light and airy while still showing the effects of age and wear. I achieved this without using transparent shaders.

# **How did Marvelous Designer fit into your workflow for this project, especially when creating believable cloth, fabric, or soft interior elements?**

Curtains played an essential role in the visual storytelling. Through fabric, you can convey how deeply abandoned a place is and even hint at the era it belongs to through the cut and style of the cloth.

At the same time, this element brings the scene to life: a gentle sway in the wind, the silhouette of natural folds, and the softness that can be achieved through simulation in Marvelous Designer.

![0738a70d1ab346c3a11366e949c50449](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/0738a70d1ab346c3a11366e949c5044903%20%281%29.png)

# **What is your favorite feature or tool to use in Marvelous Designer?**

My favorite thing about Marvelous Designer is how naturally everything comes together. You simply run the simulation, and the fabric drapes on its own, creating realistic folds and wrinkles.

I also love being able to add creases by hand, work with sewing patterns just like in real tailoring, and adjust the physical properties of each fabric. One of the biggest advantages is that the UVs stay the same as the original sewing patterns, which makes UV mapping much easier.

Being able to work directly with your own avatar also makes it easy to create custom pieces that fit your project perfectly.

# **Could you walk us through one of your curtain pipelines, from cloth simulation to the final real-time scene?**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KdKIy4SnCg8

Let me walk you through one of the pipelines I used for the curtains, probably the simplest one.

**1\. Import Avatar**

First, I imported an avatar for the cloth simulation. In my case, it was the entire wall module, which let me match the exact dimensions and make sure the curtain interacted correctly with the floor.

**2\. Base Shape**

Then I created a base curtain shape that could be reused and varied later. Saving it as a separate file is a huge time-saver, since it gives you a solid starting point for creating different variations.

**3\. Shaping, Fabric Settings & Export**

Once I was happy with the overall silhouette and design, I exported it as an FBX. I chose not to use baked animation. While Alembic is tempting, it has a noticeable impact on scene performance in Unreal Engine.

In Blender, I checked the scale, UVs, and mesh density, keeping only the geometry necessary to preserve the folds. After all, in a personal project, you're your own boss.

**4\. Texturing**

There are many ways to texture curtains. You can use tiling textures, trim sheets, or unique textures. If you plan to create many different fabric variations, a modular approach also works well.

In this project, I used a mix of all three. Some curtains use unique textures, while others use tiling materials.

**5\. Import into Unreal Engine**

Finally, I imported the curtains into Unreal Engine, set up the materials, and made the final adjustments. I also smoothed some parts of the mesh, since detailed folds on low-poly geometry can sometimes create visible aliasing.

This can be fixed in Blender, ZBrush, or directly in Unreal. The wind effect was added in Unreal Engine to keep everything lightweight and performant.

![ab220cd03d3542fba2a0cd957eb4b13f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/ab220cd03d3542fba2a0cd957eb4b13fAna%20Vien%20-%20reduced%202.png)![c32ba6868fdc454fa802d88d24edd686](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/c32ba6868fdc454fa802d88d24edd686Ana%20vien%20-%20reduced%201.png)

# **What was the most challenging part of creating _The Abandoned Orphanage_ , and what advice would you give to artists who want to use Marvelous Designer in environment art?**

The biggest challenge was finding the right balance between visual quality and performance.

My biggest piece of advice is not to think of Marvelous Designer as a tool just for making clothes. It's also a powerful tool for environment art.

You can use it to create curtains, tablecloths, bed sheets, carpets, banners, canopies, tents, and many other assets that make a scene feel more realistic and alive. Start with simple objects, and don't be afraid to experiment.

![97d723e5431c4c66a630bd15ada39e68](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/97d723e5431c4c66a630bd15ada39e68Ana%20Vien%20-%20reduced%204.png)![806ceeeefd1d4ed4bc4f93f7a2c25852](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/ad4af3d760a74352879b88ab5d0d4bc5/images/806ceeeefd1d4ed4bc4f93f7a2c25852Ana%20Vien%20-%20reduced%203.png)
content_description: This webpage showcases 3D Environment Artist Ana Vien’s creative process and techniques using Marvelous Designer to craft realistic fabric and storytelling details in her atmospheric real-time scene, *The Abandoned Orphanage*.
